sentences.text: Shri Satyam Agrawal, learned counsel for the appellant.
Shri Ajay Tamrakar, learned Government   respondent/State.
Heard on I.A.No.7862/2025, which is first application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant-Vikas.

The appellant is aggrieved of the judgment dated 05.11.2024 passed by the learned Exclusive Special Judge, POCSO Act and SC/ST Act, Betul in S.C. No.36/2021, whereby the appellant stands convicted and sentenced as under:-
 Conviction Sentence  
 Section Act Imprisonment Fine  
 450 I.P.C. R.I. for 3 years Rs.1000/- 
 506 (Part-2) I.P.C. R.I. for 2 years Rs.1000/- 
 5(L)/6 r/w POCSO Act &
 R.I. for 20 years Rs.5,000/- 
 376 (2)(N) IPC  3(2)(V),
 3(2)(Va)
 SC/ST Act L.I. Rs.5,000/- 
 R/W 3(1),
 (B) (i)(ii)
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant is innocent.
There are general and omnibus allegations.
Roshan Nirapure (PW3) has admitted that victim had a love relationship with the 2 CRA-13958-2024 appellant and even victim's mother was aware of this fact.
There is no seizure of any obscene photographs by IO.
Even the demand of Rs.50,000/- could not be substantiated.
Prosecution has not produced the first school entry register.

Though, the mother of Vikas vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39004664/
1 prosecutrix has stated that she had produced birth certificate from the Government hospital, which too has not brought on record, thus, age of victim become doubtful.

sentences.text: Dr.Rupal (PW/6) has admitted that victim had not given any history of violation of privacy.
There are good chances of success in appeal.
Hence, prayer is made to suspend execution of remaining part of the jail sentence of the appellant and to release her on bail.
Shri Ajay Tamrakar, learned Public Prosecutor supports the impugned judgment and opposes the prayer for suspension of sentence.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and considering the fact that there appears to be good chances of success in appeal, without commenting on merits of the case, we are of the considered opinion that it is a fit case to suspend the remaining part of jail sentence of appellant and release her on bail.

It is directed that on depositing of fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing personal bond to the tune of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for her appearance before the trial Court 30.04.2026 and on all subsequent dates as may be fixed by the concerned Court, the execution of remaining part of the jail sentence of appellant shall remain suspended and 3 CRA-13958-2024 she be released on bail till final disposal of this appeal.
Accordingly, I.A. No.7862/2025 is allowed and disposed of.
List the case for final hearing in Part-B of the cause list as per its turn and seniority.
Certified copy as per rules.
 (VIVEK AGARWAL) (RATNESH CHANDRA SI  JUDGE JUDGE  RS Vikas vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39004664/
